correctness.rationale: A face decomposes uniquely as a core S with induced max degree <=1, plus arbitrary eligible leaves E(S)={v!=z: v not in S or deg_G[S](v)=0}. Toggle the least eligible leaf in each Boolean fiber; each fiber is acyclic, and under reversed matched Hasse arrows core S never increases, so no cross-fiber alternating cycles. If E(S)=empty, every v≠z belongs to S and has degree exactly one; the only candidate S=V(G) is inadmissible because connected G on n>=3 with deg(z)>=2, and S=V minus {z} is unmatched iff G-z is exactly one-regular. Remove the augmented empty-face matching to retain one critical 0-cell plus optionally one critical (n-2)-simplex. Its boundary attaches to the single 0-cell; for n-2>=1 the Morse CW space is S^{n-2}, else contractible, integral homotopy. An independently written direct simplicial mod2 enumeration of 6 eligible 3-core and 104 eligible 4-core rooted connected graph cases produced zero Betti-profile mismatches; numerical enumeration is not an all-graph proof.

value.rationale: The effect of deleting exactly one pendant whisker from a completely whiskered graph is a natural sharp topological perturbation. The global all-graphs sphere/contractible dichotomy and induced one-regular (stronger than merely perfect-matchable) condition yields arbitrarily high-dimensional sphere examples on friendship cores, which are useful test cases for stability and patchwork Morse arguments.

final_claim: For every connected finite core G with n>=3 and deg(z)>=2, adding a leaf to each vertex except z gives two-independence complex sphere S^{n-2} iff the entire induced G-z is one-regular, otherwise contractible; complete whiskering is a different homotopy regime.
